claims.claim: **Suspect IVA in any sick neonate or suspected sepsis,** and at any age with faltering growth, developmental delay and recurrent illness with ketoacidosis.
claims.source_text: Isovaleric acidemia must be considered in the differential diagnosis in any neonate in poor clinical condition or with suspected sepsis, as well as in patients of any age presenting with faltering growth, developmental delay, and recurrent episodes of illness associated with ketoacidosis.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Neonatal onset:** poor feeding, vomiting and lethargy progressing to coma or seizures in the first week; a 'sweaty feet' odour can distinguish IVA from other organic acidurias.
claims.source_text: Affected newborns typically exhibit symptoms such as poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and continuous clinical deterioration to coma or seizures during the first week of life. … affected individuals may exhibit a characteristic "sweaty feet" body odor [,], which can serve as a clear distinguishing feature from other organic acidurias that otherwise have the same clinical symptoms.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Newborn screening reduces neonatal deaths in classic IVA,** but many screen-detected infants have a metabolically mild form of doubtful clinical relevance.
claims.source_text: As a preventive measure, NBS reduces neonatal mortality in patients with classic IVA. At present, it is doubtful that identification of metabolically mild forms by NBS is of any clinical relevance.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If an organic acidaemia is suspected, measure blood gases, lactate, ammonia and ketones,** plus urine organic acids and a blood acylcarnitine profile.
claims.source_text: Blood gases, lactate, ammonia, and ketone bodies should be measured if an organic acidemia including IVA is suspected. … Organic acids in urine and the acylcarnitine profile in blood should be measured if an organic acidemia including IVA is suspected.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After a positive newborn screen, urine organic acids (isovalerylglycine) are essential to confirm the diagnosis;** a raised C5-carnitine can be falsely positive after maternal pivalate-containing antibiotics.
claims.source_text: Following a positive NBS result, the analysis of organic acids in urine (IVG) is essential to confirm the diagnosis … A high number of false-positive NBS results have been documented following maternal intake of pivaloylester-containing antibiotics during the final weeks of pregnancy
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm with IVD gene sequencing and/or enzyme assay;** the c.932C>T (p.Ala311Val) variant is linked to asymptomatic, screen-detected IVA.
claims.source_text: IVD gene analysis and/or IVD enzyme assay are recommended to confirm the diagnosis of IVA. … A definite genotype-phenotype correlation is known for the common variant NM_002225.5:c.932C>T (p.Ala311Val), which has been detected in a homozygous or compound heterozygous state in a high proportion of asymptomatic individuals identified through NBS
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start treatment immediately in severe decompensation:** stop protein, promote anabolism, rehydrate, and give metabolic drug therapy.
claims.source_text: In the event of severe metabolic decompensation of an IVA patient, it is critical to initiate therapy immediately. … The emergency treatment of neonatal crises and subsequent episodes of metabolic decompensation comprises the discontinuation of protein intake, the promotion of anabolism, rehydration, and metabolic drug therapy
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV glucose 8-10 mg/kg/min in neonates and infants;** start protein-free formula orally or by tube early; add IV lipids 2 g/kg/day once a fatty-acid oxidation defect is excluded; reintroduce protein after 24 (at most 48) hours.
claims.source_text: 8 to 10 mg/kg·min of glucose are recommended for neonates and infants []. Oral intake or nasogastric tube feeding of protein-free formula should be started as early as possible. … Once a β-oxidation defect has been excluded in a symptomatic neonate, intravenous lipids at 2 g/kg·d can be introduced to further promote anabolism … After 24 (up to a maximum of 48) hours of emergency treatment, protein is reintroduced successively while monitoring ammonia concentrations and blood gases
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV L-carnitine 100 mg/kg/day** in emergencies, as for MMA and PA.
claims.source_text: Intravenous administration of 100 mg/kg·d is recommended for the emergency treatment of MMA and PA []; the same treatment is employed for patients with IVA
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hyperammonaemia usually settles as the metabolic state corrects;** carglumic acid has lowered ammonia quickly in reports. Consider extracorporeal detoxification at 250-500 µmol/L and start it at once above 500 µmol/L.
claims.source_text: A persistent tendency to hyperammonemia is less common in patients with IVA than in patients with MMA or PA, and hyperammonemia tends to resolve with correction of metabolic status and usually requires no additional specific treatment. … two retrospective investigations and one case study report a rapid and dramatic decrease in the plasma ammonia concentration in IVA patients treated with carglumic acid … extracorporeal detoxification therapy is considered in acute hyperammonemic decompensation, if the blood ammonia concentration is within the range of 250 to 500 μmol/L, and started immediately when ammonia concentrations are above 500 µmol/L
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sick days at home:** more calories and less protein (glucose polymers and/or leucine-free formula); admit if symptoms persist or worsen, and have a low threshold for young children.
claims.source_text: In case of minor illnesses, a sick day regimen with increased caloric intake and decreased protein intake can be initiated at home. If symptoms persist or worsen, the patient must be admitted to the hospital. In young children, early presentation to the hospital always needs to be considered irrespective of the clinical condition. … most effectively achieved by using oral solutions containing glucose polymers and/or leucine-free formula.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cover perioperative fasting with IV glucose** (low-protein parenteral nutrition), and IV L-carnitine 100 mg/kg/day.
claims.source_text: Peri-interventional fasting must be bridged with low protein parenteral nutrition to prevent metabolic decompensation. … During periods of fasting, glucose infusion is provided to cover the age-appropriate glucose requirement. For extended procedures or if delayed postoperative food intake is anticipated, the administration of additional intravenous lipids is reasonable (2 g/kg·d). Following a fasting period of 12 to 24 h, intravenous amino acids are administered. L-carnitine is administered intravenously at a dosage of 100 mg/kg·d.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Restrict natural protein but keep at least the FAO/WHO/UNU 2007 and EFSA 2012 minimum;** add a leucine-free amino acid supplement only if tolerance falls below that minimum.
claims.source_text: Natural protein intake should be restricted to reduce the isovaleric acid burden while ensuring that the minimum amount of protein intake recommended by FAO/WHO/UNU 2007 and EFSA 2012 is achieved. The supplementation with leucine-free L-amino acid supplements appears useful when the natural protein tolerance is below the minimum required level of protein intake.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **L-carnitine for all symptomatic IVA,** dose adjusted to keep free carnitine normal; median dose 100 mg/kg/day in two to three doses, and often much less is enough.
claims.source_text: L-carnitine is recommended for the long-term treatment of IVA, as is the case for other organic acidurias. The dosage should be individually adjusted to maintain a normal concentration of free carnitine in blood. … with a median dosage of 100 mg/kg·d [,] in two to three daily doses. Often, significantly lower doses than 100 mg/kg·d are sufficient.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Add L-glycine in metabolically severe IVA** (it forms excretable isovalerylglycine). Infant doses of 150-250 mg/kg/day are common; very high doses (300 mg/kg/day) have caused lethargy and ataxia. No study confirms its clinical benefit.
claims.source_text: Patients with metabolically severe types of IVA are additionally treated with L-glycine. There are no studies confirming the clinical effect of this therapy. … frequently used doses are 150 to 250 mg/kg·d. Generally, L-glycine supplementation is well tolerated. Encephalopathic side-effects including lethargy and ataxia may occur following the administration of exceedingly high doses of L-glycine (300 mg/kg·d)
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biochemically mild IVA needs no strict protein restriction;** carnitine is unproven there, and an emergency regimen for severe catabolic stress is the only suggested measure.
claims.source_text: Asymptomatic patients with only mild biochemical abnormalities do not have to adhere to a strict protein-restricted diet. … The efficacy of L-carnitine supplementation has not been proven in this patient group []. It is unlikely that negative effects related to a catabolic state will occur []. Patients may consider an emergency regimen during periods of severe catabolic stress [,], but refrain from any other specific therapy.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lifelong metabolic specialist and dietitian care:** plasma amino acids every 3-12 months by age, and free carnitine to adjust the L-carnitine dose.
claims.source_text: Treated patients with IVA require life-long care from both a metabolic specialist and a dietician. Laboratory investigations comprise plasma amino acid analyses every 3 to 12 months depending on the age of the patient … The free plasma carnitine concentration can guide L-carnitine therapy.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Connect symptomatic patients with a multidisciplinary developmental team** (neurology, physiotherapy, educational and speech therapy, psychology); organ-specific screening is not needed without symptoms.
claims.source_text: symptomatic patients should be connected with a multidisciplinary team comprising pediatric neurologists, physiotherapists, educational therapists, speech therapists, and child psychologists. … Currently available evidence does not indicate the necessity of organ-specific follow-up in the absence of symptoms.
claims.locator: Thimm E, Riederer A, Vockley J, Dobbelaere D, Williams M, MacDonald A, Dokoupil K, Schatz UA, Ensenauer R, International Journal of Neonatal Screening (MDPI, for the International Society for Neonatal Screening) 11(4):92, 'Practical Considerations for the Diagnosis and Management of Isovaleryl-CoA-Dehydrogenase Deficiency (Isovaleric Acidemia): Systematic Search and Review and Expert Opinions', published 10 October 2025, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijns11040092, retrieved 2026-09-23
